When I first opened the pack and looked at my keurig, I was king of confused because on a k-cup the keurig punches a hole in the top and bottom, but there was no hole on the reusable cup. I figured out you have to pull a piece down on the keurig to get the hole puncher to move out of the way. These re-usable cups seem to be of a good quality, they aren't made very cheap by any means. Heres some pics I took of putting it in my keurig. I would definitely recommend if you want to save some money!

Product is easy to use and compatibility with the 2.0 is not a problem. I wish the  filter areas were a lot smaller or just towards the bottom end. Much of the coffee in the bottom doesn't get wet enough to produce a good cup of coffee, as the water can escape halfway down the body. In no way could you produce a carafe that was semi strong. I have since, cup the top off a Kcup, added a couple more holes in the bottom, slid it in the body of the reusable and cut a filter from a paper towel. This forces the water through the entire body of grounds before exiting. In the meantime I'm searching for a different reusable filter. Unfortunately, most are designed like this one, where the filter area is too large, and doesn't brew a strong cup, let alone a carafe.
